Upper bounds — holds for every total

  • \(\mathrm{NS}_\delta(f) = O(\delta\,\mathrm{D}(f))\)
    ODonnell14 OSSS05
    Shallow decision trees are noise-stable. Equivalently, $\mathrm{NS}_{1/\mathrm{D}(f)}(f)=O(1)$.

The quantitative form of this -- Fourier growth of decision trees, $\sum_{|S|=k}|\hat f(S)| \le O(\sqrt{\mathrm{D}})^{k}$-type bounds -- is the engine behind the near-optimal quantum-vs-randomized separations [Tal20, BansalSinha21, SSW21].

see also: \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(f)\), \(\mathrm{D}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(f)\), [Tal20], \(\mathrm{forr}_k\) data/relations/05-fourier.yaml

total No bound exists #

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(\mathrm{TRIBES}_n) \to \tfrac12, \qquad \mathrm{MaxInf}(\mathrm{TRIBES}_n) = \Theta(\log n / n) \to 0\)
    witness: \(\mathrm{Tribes}_{w,s}\) KKL88 ODonnell14
    The Kahn--Kalai--Linial extremal case: the smallest maximal influence a balanced monotone function can have, together with maximal noise sensitivity.

No bound $\mathrm{NS}_\delta = O(\mathrm{MaxInf}^k)$ exists. This is the Kahn--Kalai--Linial regime and the one genuinely interesting cell of the three: $\mathrm{TRIBES}_n$ has $\mathrm{MaxInf} = \Theta(\log n / n) \to 0$ -- as small as a monotone balanced function can have it -- and is nonetheless maximally noise sensitive, $\mathrm{NS}_\delta \to \tfrac12$ for every fixed $\delta$. So vanishing maximal influence does not buy any noise stability at all. The reverse direction does hold, and tightly: see \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\) vs \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(f)\).

see also: \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(f)\), \(\mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\), \(\mathrm{I}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Tribes}_{w,s}\) data/relations/12-normalized.yaml

facts: $\mathrm{NS}_\delta(f)\ge \delta\,\mathrm{Var}(f)$ for $\delta\le 1/2$: flipping one pivotal coordinate already suffices.
$\mathrm{NS}_{1/2}(f) = \mathrm{Var}(f)/2$, the maximum, and $\mathrm{NS}_\delta$ is non-decreasing in $\delta$ on $[0,1/2]$.
$\mathrm{NS}_{1/\mathrm{D}(f)}(f) = O(1)$-type bounds: shallow decision trees are noise-stable, which is the basis of many quantum-vs-classical separations via Fourier growth.

total No bound exists #

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(\oplus_n) = \tfrac12\big(1-(1-2\delta)^n\big) \to \tfrac12, \qquad \mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(\oplus_n) = \rho^{\,n} \to 0\)
    witness: \(\oplus_n\) ODonnell14
    The ratio blows up not because the numerator grows -- it cannot, $\mathrm{NS}_\delta \le \tfrac12$ always -- but because the denominator collapses. That is the whole content of the cell.

No bound $\mathrm{NS}_\delta = O(\mathrm{Stab}_\rho^k)$ exists for any $k$ -- not because the two are unrelated, but because they are the same quantity, reparameterised: $$\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(f) = \tfrac12\big(1 - \mathrm{Stab}_{1-2\delta}(f)\big), \qquad \mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(f) = 1 - 2\,\mathrm{NS}_{(1-\rho)/2}(f),$$ an exact identity for every Boolean $f$, immediate from $\mathrm{Stab}_\rho = \sum_S \rho^{|S|}\hat f(S)^2$ and $\mathrm{NS}_\delta = \tfrac12\sum_S(1-(1-2\delta)^{|S|})\hat f(S)^2$. The relationship is affine, and the matrix records multiplicative ones, so it registers as no bound at all. Read the identity, not the cell.

see also: \(\mathrm{NS}_{\delta}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Stab}_{\rho}(f)\), \(\oplus_n\) data/relations/12-normalized.yaml
